source: Zab chos zhi khro dgongs pa rang grol las: Khro bo'i bar do 'char tshul bstan pa (the wrathful deities), pages 115–121 of the reproduction, from an undated Tibetan blockprint of the Thos grol cycle reproduced by the Buddhist Digital Resource Center as W23710 (text ga), read from the page images. It is a traditional blockprint, so no modern editor's work is involved. Two transcriptions found online, one of this print and one of another, were used to check the reading and are not the text. The page gives the print's wording and spelling. Three things are ours: the spaces between words, which Tibetan does not write; the line-end abbreviations, written out; and clear misprints corrected, each named in its note. Where another print reads differently in a way that matters, the note says so. Letters: the Wylie system (Extended Wylie for the Sanskrit words). Pronunciation: the reading style of central Tibet in the THL Simplified Phonetic Transcription (Germano and Tournadre, 2003), produced by rule from the spelling; a living reader's pronunciation will differ in places. The translation is new, made from the Tibetan. Still to do: the text has been read from one print at the resolution of an online scan, and doubtful places are marked in the notes; it has not been collated with the other blockprints.

sentences.l: You-yourself's lama's name by say, and: 'I, the between-in wandered am-because, help please-make! Compassion-by not let-go(?)!' do, and, prayer obtain(?)!
sentences.i: Call your own lama by name: 'I am wandering in the bardo: help me! Do not let me go from your compassion!' Do so, and pray.
sentences.n: The part begins on the line where 012 ended, after the call on the yidam; now the same call is made to the lama. bla ma'i mtshan nas brjod, 'say by the lama's name' (mtshan, 'name', the respectful word; brjod, 'to say'), as mtshan nas bos for the yidam. la after a verb, 'and'. bdag … 'khyams nas yod pas, 'because I am wandering', as in 012; the print has bdag, 'I', where the other recension has none. ra mda' mdzod cig, 'please give help!' (mdzod cig, the respectful command). thugs rjes, 'by (your) compassion'. ma btang zhig, 'do not let go!': btang, the past stem of gtong, 'to send, let go' (gtong / btang / gtang / thong), with ma, 'not', and zhig, which marks a command after -ng, as bzung zhig in 012; a prohibition usually has the present stem (ma gtong zhig), and the print has the past. zhig is doubtful on the image ([?]); there is no r there, so it is not bar. The other recension has ma gtang gyis la, with the future stem and no zhig; the sense is the same. No zhes closes the words: gyis, 'do!', the imperative of byed, follows them at once, 'do (this), and'. gsol ba thob cig is read, as in the parts before, as a guess for 'pray'.

sentences.l: Blood-drinker's deity-hosts (plural) to also devotion do, and, prayer obtain(?)! Aspiration-prayer this also obtain(?)!
sentences.i: Turn with devotion to the hosts of blood-drinking deities too, and pray; and make this aspiration-prayer as well:
sentences.n: The print runs khrag and 'thung together across the line join, here divided. khrag 'thung gi lha tshogs, 'the deity-hosts of the blood-drinkers', all the wrathful deities of text ga. mos ba is the print's spelling of mos pa, 'devotion'; mos ba gyis la, 'make devotion, and', as in 003. smon lam 'di yang thob cig, 'obtain(?) this aspiration-prayer too': thob cig stands here with smon lam, 'aspiration-prayer', as it stands with gsol ba, 'prayer', which supports the guess that thob cig means 'make (the prayer)'. 'di, 'this', points forward to the verse that follows.

sentences.l:
Alas! Habitual-tendencies fierce-by in-saṃsāra wandering's time,
dread-terror fearful-appearance abandoned's light-path on,
Blessed-Ones peaceful-wrathful's host by the-way lead!
Expanse-Ladies wrathful-women's host by(?) from-behind support!
The between fearful's narrow-passage from freeing I-pray;
the genuine perfect buddha's level-to bring!
sentences.i:
Alas! When I wander in saṃsāra through fierce habitual tendencies,
on the light-path that has left behind dread, terror and fearful sights
may the host of the peaceful and wrathful Blessed Ones lead the way,
may the host of wrathful Ladies of the Expanse support me from behind.
I pray you, free me from the fearful narrow passage of the bardo
and bring me to the level of a true and perfect buddha.
sentences.n: Verse: the prayer of the bardo, twenty-four lines of nine syllables (the first with kyai ma before it), each closed by ༔. Its first six lines follow the pattern of the daily prayers (004, 007, 008), with all the deities at once: the bag chags drag pos of the first line is the seventh day's (008). dngangs skrag 'jigs snang, 'dread, terror and fearful appearance', as in 003. spangs pa'i, 'that has abandoned' (spangs, the past stem of spong, 'to give up', + -pa'i): the light-path is free of fear. spangs is doubtful on the image ([?]). bcom ldan, 'Blessed One', here for the whole host; zhi khro'i tshogs kyis, 'by the host of the peaceful and wrathful'. dbyings phyug, 'Lady of the Expanse', the name of the consort in the daily prayers, here for the wrathful female deities as a host (khro mo, 'wrathful woman'). tshogs kyi has kyi, 'of', where the line before has kyis, 'by'; it is taken as standing for kyis, as in the prayer of 008. The last two lines are those of the daily prayers: bsgral du gsol, 'I pray that you free', bsgral the future stem of sgrol; skyol, the imperative of skyel, 'bring!'.

sentences.l:
Dear's friends from parted, then, alone-ly wander;
self-appearance empty's images dawning time this-at,

sentences.i:
Parted from dear friends, I wander alone.
Now, when the empty images of my own appearance dawn,
buddhas, send forth the force of your compassion,
that the dread, terror and fears(?) of the bardo may not arise.
sentences.n: The print has སངས་རྒྱས་རྒྱས (sangs rgyas rgyas), a misprint for སངས་རྒྱས (sangs rgyas), corrected here. rgyas is set at the end of p. 116 and again after the ornament at the head of p. 117, a word set twice across the page turn. Corrected, the third line has eight syllables, one short of the metre; the other recension's line has nine, sangs rgyas rnams kyis thugs rjes shugs phyungs nas, 'the buddhas, having sent forth the force by compassion', with kyis and rjes, 'by', and nas, 'having'. dga' ba'i grogs, 'friends one delights in' (dga' ba, 'delight'; grogs, 'friend'); dang bral nas, 'parted from' (bral, 'to be separated', takes dang). gcig pur, 'alone' (gcig pu, 'single one', + -r); the other recension has gcig par, with the same sense. rang snang, 'one's own appearance', as in 003; stong pa'i gzugs brnyan, 'images of emptiness', images (gzugs brnyan, 'reflection, image') that are empty. 'char dus 'dir, 'at this time of dawning'. shugs, 'force, impetus', is doubtful on the image ([?]). phyungs, the imperative of 'byin, 'to bring out' ('byin / phyung / dbyung / phyungs). 'jigs nga is kept as printed, as one word with its doubtful second syllable, and is uncertain: nga, doubtful on the image ([?]), is not a word here. The line wants a syllable such as snang, giving 'jigs snang, 'fearful appearances', as two lines before, or pa, giving 'jigs pa, 'fear', as the other recension has; the translation reads 'fears'. mi 'byung shog, 'may (it) not arise': shog, the imperative of 'ong, 'to come', closes a wish, 'may it be'; mi, 'not', stands before 'byung.

sentences.l:
Wisdom bright's lights five dawning time this-at,
not fearing, not terrified, own-face knowing may-I!
Peaceful and wrathful-ones' body-forms dawning time this-at,
fearless confidence obtained, the between face-know may-I!
sentences.i:
Now, when the five bright lights of wisdom dawn,
may I know them as my own face, without fear or terror.
Now, when the forms of the peaceful and wrathful ones dawn,
may I gain fearless confidence and recognise the bardo.
sentences.n: 'od lnga, 'the five lights', the lights of the five wisdoms of the peaceful days. mi 'jigs mi skrag, 'not fearing, not terrified'. rang ngo shes par shog, 'may (I) know (them) as my own face', with shes par, 'to know', before shog. zhi dang khro bo, 'the peaceful and the wrathful ones'. sku gzugs, 'bodily form' (sku, 'body', respectful; gzugs, 'form'), here the forms in which the deities appear. mi 'jigs gdengs, 'fearless confidence' (gdengs, 'confidence, assurance'); thob, 'gained', 'having gained'. bar do ngo shes, 'recognise the bardo', know it for what it is.

Bad-karma power's suffering experiencing when,
yidam deity by(?) suffering dispelling may-it!
Reality-itself's own-sound, thunders thousand roaring when,
all six-syllable sound-into turning may-it!
sentences.i:
When I suffer through the power of bad karma,
may my yidam deity dispel the suffering.
When the own sound of reality roars like a thousand thunders,
may it all become the sound of the six syllables.
sentences.n: las ngan dbang gi sdug bsngal, 'the suffering of the power of bad karma', suffering that comes by its power. myong, 'to experience, to undergo'; tsa na, 'when', after the verb (as de tsa na, 'at that time', in the earlier parts). yi dam lha yi: yi is the 'of' ending after a vowel, used in verse; 'of the yidam deity' gives no sense before sdug bsngal sel, 'dispel the suffering', so it is taken for yis, 'by', as in the daily prayer of 004; the other recension has yis here, and dbang gis, 'by the power', for dbang gi in the line before. sel bar shog, 'may (it) dispel' (sel, 'to clear away'). chos nyid rang sgra, 'the own sound of reality', and 'brug stong, 'a thousand thunders', as in 003 and 008; ldir, 'to roar, boom'. yig drug, 'the six syllables', a mantra of six syllables; the text does not name it (usually the six-syllable mantra of Avalokiteśvara). sgra ru, 'into the sound' (ru, 'into', after a vowel); 'gyur bar shog, 'may (it) turn'.

sentences.l:
Refuge without, karma's after following time this-at,
compassion great-by me to protecting I-pray!
Habitual-tendencies' karma's suffering experiencing when,
clear-light bliss's absorption dawning may-it!
sentences.i:
Now, when without refuge I follow after my karma,
I pray you, protect me with your great compassion.
When I undergo the suffering of the karma of my habitual tendencies,
may the absorption of clear light and bliss dawn.
sentences.n: The print has ཆེན་པས (chen pas), a misprint for ཆེན་པོས (chen pos), corrected here. No o-sign can be seen on the image ([?]) in a crowded line, and only chen pos, 'by the great (compassion)', gives sense; the image reading is moderately certain. skyabs med, 'without refuge' (skyabs, 'refuge'; med, 'there is not'). las kyi rjes su 'brang, 'follow after karma', go where it drives ('brang, 'to follow', the present stem, past 'brangs). skyab tu gsol, 'I pray that you protect', on the pattern of bsgral du gsol: skyab is taken as a spelling of bskyab, the future stem of skyob, 'to protect' (skyob / bskyabs / bskyab / skyobs), which the other recension has. bag chags las kyi, 'of the karma of habitual tendencies'. The print sets the prefix 'a small under the cha (ཆཱར), a contraction of 'char; written out here. 'od gsal bde ba'i ting 'dzin, 'the absorption of clear light and bliss' (bde ba, 'bliss'; ting 'dzin, short for ting nge 'dzin, 'meditative absorption', Sanskrit samādhi); 'char bar shog, 'may (it) dawn'.

sentences.l:
Five-elements' realms (plural) sound-as not rise, and,
buddhas five-families' realms seeing may-I!
sentences.i:
May the realms of the five elements not rise up as sound(?),
and may I see the realms of the buddhas of the five families.
sentences.n: The last two lines of the prayer. 'byung lnga, 'the five elements', earth, water, fire, wind and space ('byung ba, 'element'); 'byung lnga'i khams, 'the realms of the five elements' (khams, 'realm, element'), the realms or forces they make up. sgra ru mi ldang zhing, 'not rise up as sound, and' (ldang, 'to rise up'; zhing, 'and', after -ng). The sense is not sure: the line before has sgra ru, 'into the sound', and the words are taken as printed; the other recension has sdang, 'to be hostile', for ldang, which points to the elements rising up against the dead person. sgra ru may stand for dgra ru, 'as enemies' (dgra ru ldang, 'to rise up as an enemy'), which would give that sense with ldang; the image, checked enlarged, plainly has sgra, and nothing is changed. rigs lnga'i zhing khams, 'the realms of the five families', the pure lands of the five buddhas of the peaceful days; mthong bar shog, 'may (I) see'.

sentences.l: Terror-fright all faded, then, certainly enjoyment-body-as buddha-being becomes-because, important-is. Not be-distracted! So, times three or seven's until is-said.
sentences.i: All terror and fright will fade, and he will surely become a buddha in the body of enjoyment; so this is important. Do not be distracted! This is said three times, or up to seven.
sentences.n: 'jigs skrag, 'terror, fright'. yal, 'to fade, vanish'; yal nas, 'having faded, then'. longs skur, 'as the body of enjoyment' (longs sku, short for longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku, 'body of perfect enjoyment', as in 006, + -r): the radiant body of the peaceful and wrathful deities. sangs rgyas par 'gyur bas, 'because (he) becomes a buddha'. gal che'o, 'it is important' (gal che, 'the stake is great', + the sentence-ending -'o). ma yengs shig, 'do not be distracted!', as in 002. ces, 'so', closes the reader's words; lan gsum 'am bdun gyi bar du, 'up to three or seven times' ('am, 'or', here written as its own syllable after gsum; bar du, 'until, up to'). brjod do, 'is said' (brjod, 'to say', + the sentence-ending -do).

sentences.l: He, as-for: sin however great, and, karmic-residue however bad though, not freed not possible-is.
sentences.i: However great his sins and however bad his karmic residue, it cannot be that he is not freed.
sentences.n: de ni, 'as for him', the dead person for whom the prayer is said; the other recension has des ni, 'by that', the prayer, as the means of freeing, and adds ni after las 'phro. sdig pa, 'sin, evil deed'. ji ltar che zhing, 'however great, and' (zhing, 'and', links the two clauses); ji ltar ngan yang, 'however bad, still'. las 'phro, 'karmic residue', as in the earlier parts. mi grol mi srid do, 'that (he) is not freed is not possible': two negatives make a strong yes (srid, 'to be possible').

sentences.l: These (plural) however done though, face not meeting if, as-for: the between third, becoming's the between-in wander must-because, that's face-introduction below in-detail is-shown.
sentences.i: If, however all this is done, he still does not recognise, he must wander in the third bardo, the bardo of becoming; so its pointing-out is shown in detail below.
sentences.n: 'di rnams ji ltar byas kyang, 'however these are done' (byas, the past stem of byed). ngo ma 'phrod na ni, 'if the face is not met', if he does not recognise (ma … na, 'if not'; ni sets off the condition). bar do gsum pa, 'the third bardo', after the bardo of the moment of death and the bardo of reality; srid pa'i bar do, 'the bardo of becoming', as in 009, the subject of text ja. 'khyams dgos pas, 'because (he) must wander' (dgos, 'must, be needed', + -pas, 'because'). pas is doubtful on the image ([?]); it may be bas, with the same sense. de'i ngo sprod, 'its pointing-out'. 'og tu, 'below, later on'; 'og is doubtful on the image ([?]). zhib par, 'in detail'. bstan to, 'is shown': bstan, the past and future stem of ston, 'to show', with the sentence-ending -to.

sentences.l: In-general, practice great-small whichever to also, death-point-at a-little being-confused many-are-because, Hearing-Liberation this without's means is-not.
sentences.i: In general, whether one's practice is great or small, many are somewhat confused at the moment of death; so there is no doing without this Liberation through Hearing.
sentences.n: spyir, 'in general', is doubtful on the image ([?]); it may be phyir. gom pa is the print's spelling of goms pa, 'familiarity, practice' (goms, 'to get used to'), as gom 'dris in the next sentence; the other recension has these two words the other way round. che chung, 'great or small' (che, 'great'; chung, 'small'); gang la yang, 'for whichever'. 'chi khar, 'at the moment of death'. bag re, 'a little, somewhat'; 'khrul ba, 'to be confused, mistaken'; mang bas, 'because (they) are many'. med pa'i thabs med, 'there is no way of being without (it)', as in 009.

sentences.l: Familiarity great-ones (plural) to, matter-knowing parted, then, reality-itself in-a-flash(?) comes.
sentences.i: For those whose familiarity is great, once body and awareness have parted, reality comes at once.
sentences.n: The print writes 'ong ngo as one contracted syllable (འོངོ), written out here. Its first letter is doubtful on the image ([?]): it may be yong ngo, with the same sense, 'comes'. gom 'dris, 'familiarity through practice' (goms, 'get used to'; 'dris, 'be well acquainted'), spelled gom as in the sentence before. bem rig, 'matter and awareness' (bem po, 'inert matter', the body; rig pa, 'awareness'); bral nas, 'having parted', at death. lam gyis is taken as 'in a flash' and written as one word, as in the pilot and 002 (unit 36); read as two words, lam, 'path', with gyis, 'by', it could also be 'by the path', as in 002 (unit 49).

sentences.l: Alive's time-at knowing-top-on face met-ones and; experience having-ones (plural), as-for: dying-point's the between-in clear-light dawned's power very great-is-because, living's time-at practice important-is.
sentences.i: For those who have recognised it in awareness itself while alive, and for those who have experience, the clear light dawns with very great power in the bardo of the moment of death; so practice while one is alive is important.
sentences.n: The print has གསོན་པོས (gson pos), a misprint for གསོན་པོའི (gson po'i), corrected here. The instrumental gives no sense before dus su, and the same phrase is printed correctly twice on this page (gson po'i dus su) and in the other recension; the image reading is moderately certain. gson po'i dus su, 'at the time of being alive' (gson po, 'alive'). rig thog tu, 'on awareness', right in awareness itself (rig, short for rig pa; thog tu, 'upon'). ngo 'phrod pa, 'one whose face is met', who has recognised. nyams myong, 'meditative experience'; yod pa, 'one who has'. 'chi kha'i bar do, 'the bardo of the moment of death', the first bardo. The print runs ba'i and stobs together across the line join, here divided. 'od gsal shar ba'i stobs, 'the power of the clear light's dawning'; shin tu che bas, 'because (it) is very great'. gson pa'i, 'of the living', the print's other spelling beside gson po'i. nyams len, 'practice', as in 002.

sentences.l: Again, alive's time-at secret-mantra's deity's generation-completion meditating-ones (plural), as-for: reality-itself the between from, peaceful-wrathful's appearances dawned's time-at, power very great-ly there-is.
sentences.i: Again, those who meditated on the generation and completion of the deities of secret mantra while alive have very great power when the appearances of the peaceful and wrathful ones dawn in the bardo of reality.
sentences.n: The print runs bsgom and pa together across the line join, here divided. gsang sngags kyi lha, 'the deity of secret mantra', the deity of tantric practice. bskyed rdzogs, 'generation and completion', the two stages of tantric meditation, as in 009; bsgom pa, 'meditating' (bsgom, the future stem of sgom, + -pa), here 'those who meditate'. chos nyid bar do las, 'in the bardo of reality': las, 'from, out of', marks the bardo as the place from which the appearances dawn; the other recension has la, 'in'. Three vowel signs in this line are hidden by strokes from the line above, so do in bar do, khro'i and gson in the next sentence are doubtful ([?]); each is read as the sense and the words around it require. stobs … che bar yod do, 'there is great power' (che bar, 'great', with -r; yod do, 'there is').

sentences.l: Therefore, alive's time-at also, Between Hearing-Liberation this especially mind in trained-ly making, as-for: very important-is.
sentences.i: Therefore, while one is alive too, it is very important above all to learn this Liberation in the Bardo through Hearing by heart.
sentences.n: de bas na, 'therefore', a set phrase (de, 'that'; bas, 'than, from', the ending of comparison; na, 'then'): 'from that, then'. gson is doubtful on the image ([?]). bar do thos grol, 'the Liberation in the Bardo through Hearing', the full name of the book. yid la byang bar byed pa, 'to make (it) trained in the mind', to know it by heart (byang, 'trained, purified'). sentences.l: Great-adept Nyi-zla-sangs-rgyas's sons' eldest, accomplished-one Karma-Gling-pa-by: river Gser-ldan's bank, Sgam-po-bdar's mountain, gods(?) servants(?) dance doing like's place from, secretly, and, invited-out-is.
sentences.i: The eldest son of the great adept Nyi zla sangs rgyas, the accomplished Karma Gling pa, brought it out in secret from a place on the bank of the river Gser ldan, on the mountain of Sgam po bdar, which looks like gods and servants dancing(?).
sentences.n: The colophon. An extra ༔ before grub chen opens it. grub chen, 'great adept' (grub, 'accomplishment'; chen, 'great'); grub thob, below, 'one who has gained accomplishment' (Sanskrit siddha). Nyi zla sangs rgyas, 'Sun-Moon Buddha', a personal name. sras kyi thu bo, 'the eldest of the sons' (sras, 'son', respectful; thu bo, 'eldest'). Karma Gling pa, with -s, 'by', marking who brought the text out; the text says no more of him than this. chu bo gser ldan, 'the river Gser ldan' ('golden'); 'gram, 'bank'. Sgam po bdar, a place name; bdar is doubtful on the image ([?]), and the other recension has gdar; the print is kept. lha bran gar byed pa 'dra ba'i gnas, 'a place like gods(?) and servants(?) making a dance' (gar, 'dance'; 'dra ba, 'like'): the shape of the mountain, it seems; the words are clear but the sense is not sure. The other recension has ri bo ri lha bran gyis gar byed pa, with ri lha, 'mountain god', and gyis, 'by', marking who dances; so ri lha may belong together here too, 'like the mountain god's servants(?) making a dance'. gnas nas, 'from the place', where the other recension has gter nas, 'from the treasure'; the print is kept. gsang ste, 'secretly' (gsang, 'secret'; ste, 'and'). gdan drangs pa'o, 'was invited, brought out' (gdan drangs, the respectful 'invite', drangs the past of 'dren, 'to lead'), with the sentence-ending -'o: the word for bringing out a treasure text as if inviting a guest.

sentences.l: He-by, son Chos-rje-Gling-pa to, word and transmission entrusted. His guru Sūrya-candra to, in-sequence, word and transmission descended is.
sentences.i: He entrusted the word and the transmission to his son Chos rje Gling pa; and from him, in sequence, the word and the transmission came down to Guru Sūryacandra.
sentences.n: des, 'by him', Karma Gling pa. sras, 'son'; Chos rje Gling pa, his son's name (chos rje, 'lord of the teaching', a title). bka', 'word', the teaching itself; lung, 'transmission', the authorisation given by reading the text aloud to the disciple. gtad, the past stem of gtod, here 'to hand over, to entrust'. The plain stroke ། closes the clause. de'i, 'his', where the other recension has des, 'by him'. Read as printed, de'i gu ru, 'his guru', would make Sūryacandra the teacher of Chos rje Gling pa; but the word comes down (babs) to him, from one to the next (rim par, 'in sequence', which the print adds), so the idiomatic line reads de'i as des, 'from him', and gu ru as Sūryacandra's title. gu ru, Sanskrit guru, 'teacher', in Tibetan letters; Sūryacandra, 'Sun-Moon', in Sanskrit, written su rya tsandra (su rya doubtful on the image, [?]); the other recension has a longer name, with rasmi, 'ray'. babs pa, 'came down' (babs, the past of 'bab, 'to descend'); lags so, 'is', the respectful word.

sentences.l: His presence-in, I, Gha-gha-dharma-pa-mu-dra-by, respectfully requested.
sentences.i: In his presence I, Gha gha dharma pa mu dra, respectfully received it.
sentences.n: The scribe speaks. de'i drung du, 'in his presence' (drung, 'nearness, presence'). bdag, 'I', the humble word. Gha gha dharma pa mu dra, the scribe's name, half in Sanskrit letters, with -s, 'by'; pa and dras are doubtful on the image ([?]), and the other recension spells it ga ga dharma pa mu dras. gus par, 'respectfully'. zhus, the past of zhu, 'to ask, to request', the humble verb: to ask for a teaching and receive it. The print writes zhus so as one contracted syllable (ཞུསོ), written out here; a lone ༔ at the far end of the line is a filler mark and is left out. The print has no closing dedication, where the other recension has one (beginning 'di bris dge bas, 'by the merit of writing this'). Here the text, and the Great Liberation through Hearing, end.

about: The last part of text ga, and the end of the Great Liberation through Hearing. It finishes the call for help: the dead person is to call his own lama by name, ask not to be let go from his compassion, turn with devotion to the blood-drinking deities too, and make the prayer of the bardo. The prayer follows in twenty-four lines of verse. It begins as the daily prayers began, asking the peaceful and wrathful hosts to lead the way through the narrow pass of the bardo, and goes on through what the dead person meets there: wandering alone without friends, the empty images of his own appearance, the five lights, the forms of the deities, the roar of reality's own sound, the pull of karma; for each it asks that fear not arise and that he recognise what he sees. Said three or seven times with strong devotion, the text says, the prayer cannot fail to free him, however great his sins. Whoever is still not freed must go on to the third bardo, the bardo of becoming, which is taught later. Then the benefits of the book: even those well practised are confused at death, so no one can do without it; those who have practised in life have great power when the clear light and the deities dawn, so it is to be learned, read and kept in mind while alive. Heard even by one who has committed the five worst crimes, it frees him; heard once now and not understood, it will be remembered in the bardo, where awareness is nine times clearer. It is to be read in crowds, at the heads of the sick and beside the dead, and to meet it at all is great good fortune. The text closes with its title and a colophon: Karma Gling pa, eldest son of the adept Nyi zla sangs rgyas, brought it out in secret near the river Gser ldan; it passed to his son Chos rje Gling pa and in time to Guru Sūryacandra, from whom the scribe, Gha gha dharma pa mu dra, received it.
